qualification: Use the output as an estimate, not a promise of zero uncertainty.
method: Distinguish the meaning of estimation from a guarantee of exactness; the source supplies no zero-noise or perfect-model assumption.

sourceClaim: Global planning computes an optimal path offline before movement starts.
qualification: Treat this as the lecture’s comparison, not a universal prohibition on online global replanning.
method: Apply the explicitly supplied whole-map replanning scenario and separate spatial planning scope from execution timing.

sourceClaim: Edge weights help determine the absolute best path based on real-world constraints.
qualification: Best means minimum modeled cost for the declared objective and feasible represented routes, not every objective at once.
method: Compare two different meanings of the edge weights explicitly listed by the source.

sourceClaim: Randomly hopping between neighboring vertices has no guarantee of reaching the goal.
qualification: The generic warning must be distinguished from this particular finite directed acyclic graph, whose every A-started outgoing walk reaches E.
method: Enumerate the five directed A-to-E paths and observe that all branches terminate at E within four moves.

sourceClaim: UCS is an optimal graph-search algorithm.
qualification: The lecture’s positive-distance example satisfies the required nonnegative-edge setting. Do not extend the guarantee to arbitrary negative edge costs.
method: Trace the fully specified acyclic negative-edge counterexample using the source’s cumulative-cost priority and goal-on-removal rule.

sourceClaim: A* uses a heuristic to reach the optimal path faster than UCS.
qualification: The example establishes an expansion-count advantage, not an unconditional elapsed-time guarantee.
method: Compare the printed node counts and equal route costs, then use f=g when h=0 as a counterexample to universal strict search reduction.

method: Compare all source heuristic labels with exact remaining costs, and test h(u)≤c(u,v)+h(v). General implementation conditions are explanatory qualifications, not asserted as printed course content.
